LESSON: READING 12.4.1: SHORT STORY: CHARACTERS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What qualities do you admire in people?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the characters in the short story
2. write a paragraph on the characters in the short story

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the characters in the short story
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the characters in the short story. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. write a paragraph on the characters in the short story
   In simple words: practise until you can write a paragraph on the characters in the short story. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters.
4. Show that you can: identify the characters in the short story

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a story in print or non-print form,
2. Read a short story and discuss the actions and words of the characters in the story,
3. Write paragraphs describing the traits of the characters in the short story using different words and expressions,
4. Role play the different characters in the short story bringing out their traits,
5. Critical thinking: It is developed as the learner analyses characters in the short story.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What qualities do you admire in people?
2. How can character traits be described?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the characters in the short story
2. write a paragraph on the characters in the short story

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
